t19: A random selection wheel is the simplest tool to end a "who should do it" and "which one will it be" argument in three seconds. Building it takes a minute — but there's a real difference between a well-built wheel and a poorly built one.
t20: Four steps to build a wheel
t22: One option per slice. Keep it short; long text doesn't read on a spinning wheel.
t24: Fewer is unnecessary, more becomes hard to read.
t26: If some options should come up more often, increase the slice width.
t28: Rebuilding the same wheel every week is the most time-wasting step.
t30: The wheels built most often are below; you can copy them directly.
t32: home cooking · order in · go out · use leftovers · toast
t38: take notes · present · coffee · weekend duty
t42: action · comedy · horror · documentary (then second wheel for the movie)
t44: On an equally sliced wheel, every option comes up with the same probability. This is right for raffles, but not true to life for daily decisions: a place you go three times a week shouldn't have the same chance as one you visit once a year.
t45: When you apply weight, a slice's probability equals the area it covers. Weights of 4-2-1-1 total 8 units; the first option comes up 50%, the second 25%, the others 12.5%.
t47: Some decisions don't fit in one wheel. For "what should we watch?" you pick a genre first, then a movie from that genre. In nested wheels, the first wheel's result determines the second wheel's content; this way you don't have to squeeze 40 options into one wheel.
t49: If you want to set an order rather than pick a single winner, turn on elimination mode: the picked option is removed from the wheel and doesn't come back. This is the right tool for presentation order, game order, or duty distribution.
t50: In normal mode, all options are in the pool on every spin; the same result can come up in a row and that's perfectly normal.
t52: Spinning again if you don't like the result.
t53: This erases all benefit of the tool. An option you don't want should never be on the wheel.
t55: A 15-slice wheel becomes as exhausting as deciding itself.
t57: The wheel is a speed tool for small, reversible decisions.
t59: Spinify combines 14 ready-made wheel templates, per-slice weight settings, nested wheels, and elimination mode in one app. Save the wheel you build and use the same one each week.
t61: How do you make a random selection wheel?
t62: Enter options one by one, keep the count between 3–8, add weight to slices if needed, and save the wheel. Setup takes less than a minute.
t63: Is a selection wheel truly random?
t64: A slice's probability to come up equals the area it covers on the wheel. With equal slices all options have the same probability; with weighted slices they come up in the ratios you set.
t65: How do I prevent the same option from coming up again?
t66: Turn on elimination mode. The picked option is removed from the wheel, and the remaining slices' probabilities automatically redistribute.
